Seated cuff on Day 0 at 08:05: SBP 126, DBP 78, pulse 60 bpm. Watch steps 2500, 2300 and 2100 on Day -2, Day -1 and Day 0. Wear time 93%; device-quality flag: watch strap re-seated Day -1. Adult child: she says she feels normal and is cooking; she asks whether the watch has got it wrong again.
cases.rationale: Two devices disagree by 12 to 13 bpm on the same mornings, with the watch at 57-59 bpm and the ring at 70-72 bpm, starting two days after verapamil SR was raised from 80 mg to 120 mg, so the disagreement sits exactly where a rate-slowing dose change would show. The cuff pulse of 60 bpm on Day 0 sides with the watch, but the ring reads higher, so the true resting rate is not settled by any one device. The patient reports feeling normal, cuff SBP is 126, and no rate below 45 bpm is recorded, so no hard trigger applies and no page is needed. The right route is a nurse task within 24 hours to take a manual pulse and a short rhythm check, with an ECG strip requested to settle which device is accurate before the rate drug is judged. Naive-model trap: a shallow model sees a device disagreement with no symptoms and files silent_log with a ticket, missing that after a rate-slowing dose change the disagreement changes the nurse's next decision.
cases.decisive_feature: Watch resting HR 57-59 against ring 70-72 on the same mornings, starting two days after verapamil SR was raised from 80 to 120 mg.

tally.notes: Module focus: LX8-001 to LX8-008 (6 drift cases, 2 single-stream cases) in focus; LX8-009 and LX8-010 are outside focus (20%). The module asks for at most 15% outside focus and also for at least 30% outside; these conflict, so the explicit drift 6 and single_stream 2 minimums were kept. DO_NOT_REPEAT contained blank entries, which were ignored. The list was checked for overlap, and each decisive_feature was written to differ from it. No near-miss pairs are required at N=10, so none were built.
